newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end down on low volume.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end down on low volume.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended slightly weaker on low volumes Friday, with the complex continuing to lack much sense of direction as the year winds down, traders said.
"The market is not showing any major turning point yet," said Scott Meyers of Pioneer Futures Inc in New York.
"Fundamentally there is little to suggest gold should go higher, as central bank and producer selling is still hanging over the market and physical demand is soft," he said.
"But the gold market often sees some gains early in the new year," he said.
COMEX February gold ended down 40 cents at $370.40, after trading in a narrow $371.90-370.20 range on estimated total volume of 15,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $368.45/368.95, down from the London Friday afternoon fix at $369.00, and the New York close Thursday at $368.90/369.40.
COMEX March silver closed down 1.0 cent at $4.850 an ounce, after seeing a $4.895-4.830 range on estimated total volume of 9,000 lots.
COMEX January gold and silver options expired Friday but open interest was low as January is not an active month.
"Implied volatilties are up on a few weeks back, but are still nothing to write home about," Meyers said.
"In fact activity is so light right now, some of the locals are leaving the ring to trade oil and natgas," he said.
"The low volatility of late means it's a difficult trading market and a poor investment market."
Precious metals have been consolidating in the past 10 days after spot gold slid to a three year low at $366.00 an ounce at the end of November.
But the complex has also received some support from volatility in stock and bond markets in the past week.
"Investors remain fixated by conditions in the equity and bond markets and are ignoring precious metals for the moment," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
NYMEX January platinum ended down 30 cents at $370.90 an ounce, while NYMEX March palladium closed down 65 cents at $119.75.
Platinum remained the weakest contract in the complex, with the April platinum/April gold spread ending up slightly at $1.10 an ounce, after sliding from $9.40 on November 21.
News of problems in the annual contract negotiations between the Russians and Japanese over 1997 contract sales of platinum was causing nervousness in the platinum group metals markets, traders said.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk,+1-212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
